# Hermes Agent — Onboarding & Troubleshooting FAQ

---

### 1. Installation & Environment

#### Platform Support
- **Native Windows (10/11):** Supported out of the box via the PowerShell installer (`install.ps1`). Note that running the Web Dashboard embedded terminal (`/chat`) requires a POSIX PTY; use WSL2 if you need the embedded terminal pane.
- **Docker / NAS (UGOS, Synology, unRAID):** When encountering `[Errno 13] Permission denied` on mounted paths like `/opt/data/config.yaml`, pass `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) environment variables to map file ownership properly.
- **Docker ARM64 / Raspberry Pi / Apple Silicon:** Multi-arch images (`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`) are natively published.
- **Android / Termux:** Supported out of the box via `scripts/install.sh`, using the curated `.[termux-all]` package bundle and `$TMPDIR`.

#### Update Process
- Run `hermes update` to update dependencies and pull upstream commits.
- If the Node.js dependency update appears stuck, it is usually Camofox quietly downloading browser binaries in the background.

---

### 2. User Interface & Dashboards

- **Web Dashboard:** Hermes includes an official web UI. Launch it with `hermes dashboard` to open `http://127.0.0.1:9119`. The **Chat** tab embeds the full Hermes TUI into your browser.
- **Open WebUI Streaming:** Hermes streams OpenAI-compatible chat completions. Live tool progress events are forwarded via SSE unless explicitly filtered out.

---

### 3. Model Providers & Authentication

#### Local Models (Ollama / LocalAI)
- **Small Models Running Slow (4B–9B):** Tool schemas (~45 tools) use many tokens per turn. Speed up performance by running `hermes tools` to disable unused toolsets, applying faster quantizations, using 32B+ models, or setting `terminal.backend: local`.
- **Provider Routing Override:** If `provider: auto` routes requests to remote providers (e.g. Anthropic) due to existing environment variables, force your local endpoint in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
  ```yaml
  model:
    default: ollama/your-model
    provider: custom
    base_url: http://localhost:11434
  fallback_providers: []
  ```
- **Ollama Cloud:** Use provider `ollama-cloud` with the endpoint `https://ollama.com/v1`.
- **Token Usage Tracking:** Streaming calls to OpenAI-compatible endpoints automatically forward `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`.
- **Vision Support on Custom Models:** Set `supports_vision: true` under your custom model configuration.

#### Cloud & Third-Party Providers
- **Anthropic / Claude Code:** Passing an API key bills usage to your API balance. To use a Pro/Max subscription allowance, authenticate via OAuth.
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Run `hermes setup` to auto-detect `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL` or configure `provider: azure-foundry`.
- **Google Gemini:** Use Google AI Studio with `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`. Legacy CLI OAuth flows are not supported.
- **DeepSeek:** Ensure model names in configuration are passed cleanly as `deepseek-v4-flash` or `deepseek-v4-pro` rather than generic aliases.

#### Model Routing Policy
- Hermes maintains the session's designated model and provider throughout a turn. Complexity-based automatic model routing (e.g. `smart_model_routing`) is not supported. Subagents use `delegation.provider` / `delegation.model` in `config.yaml`.

---

### 4. Messaging Gateways (Discord, Telegram, Matrix, DingTalk, Email, Weixin)

#### Interactive Setup & Configuration
- Run `hermes gateway setup` to launch an interactive wizard for Discord, Telegram, and other messaging platforms.

#### Authorization & Access Control
- **Unauthorized User Errors in Telegram:** `allowed_chats` filters group chats, not individual DMs. To authorize DM users, use one of the following in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
  ```yaml
  telegram:
    allow_from: "123456789"    # Comma-separated user IDs (TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS)
    # allow_all: true          # Alternatively allow all users (TELEGRAM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS)
  ```
- **Pairing Approval:** Users can DM the bot to receive a pairing code, which you approve via CLI:
  ```bash
  hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>
  ```

#### Attachments & Media Handling
- **File Uploads to the Agent:** Authorized uploads of text or code (`.py`, `.txt`, etc.) across platforms (e.g. Discord) are cached and injected directly into context.
- **Agent File Delivery:** The agent sends generated local files directly through gateway channels (Matrix `m.file`, SMTP email multipart attachments, Telegram images, etc.).
- **DingTalk Images:** Markdown image links (`![image](url)`) are formatted for rich-text delivery.
- **MCP Tool Images:** Images generated by MCP tools are tagged (`MEDIA:<path>`) and automatically forwarded as native media.

#### Multi-Profile & Multi-Agent Gateways
- **Multiple Accounts / Gateways:** Multiplexed gateway mode (`gateway/run.py`) runs multiple platform accounts (e.g. multiple Weixin or Discord accounts) under isolated profiles and credential scopes.
- **Per-Channel Personas:** Set `channel_prompts` in your platform configuration to give the bot unique personas across different channels/groups:
  ```yaml
  discord:
    channel_prompts:
      "CHANNEL_ID": "You are an IT support assistant."
  ```

---

### 5. Memory, Goals, & Autonomous Execution

#### Memory Architecture
- **`SOUL.md`:** Defines the persistent identity and persona of the agent.
- **`USER.md`:** Stores user profile preferences and facts (`target="user"`).
- **`MEMORY.md`:** Stores general project/agent knowledge.
- **Honcho Memory Backend:** Local Honcho instances do not require an API key; pointing `base_url` to `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` automatically activates local mode.
- **Custom Memory Providers:** In-tree additions to `plugins/memory/` are closed. Custom memory engines must be installed as external plugins in `~/.hermes/plugins/`.

#### Long-Running Tasks & Autonomy
- **Turn Limits:** The default turn limit is controlled by `agent.max_turns` (default 90). Override per conversation with `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`.
- **`/goal` (Persistent Execution):** For tasks requiring multiple iterations across turn limits, use `/goal`. It runs persistent autonomous execution across turns and can be resumed with `/goal resume`.
- **Session Continuity:** Sessions interrupted by restarts are preserved in `resume_pending` status and can be restored with `/resume`. Automatic idle resets are disabled by default (`mode: none`).
- **Context Management:** Token windows are optimized via `agent/context_compressor.py`, pruning verbose past tool results while preserving the recent conversation tail.

---

### 6. Tools, Plugins, & Observability

#### Custom Tools & Plugins
- Personal/custom tools should be created as plugins in `~/.hermes/plugins/` and enabled with:
  ```bash
  hermes plugins enable <plugin-name>
  ```
- Register tools inside plugin code via `ctx.register_tool(...)`.

#### Subagents
- Spawning subagents is handled via the `delegate_task` tool, running isolated context windows and toolsets (up to 3 concurrent tasks by default).

#### Observability & Skill Usage
- **Langfuse Integration:** Enable call-chain tracing and parameter inspection via `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.
- **Skill Usage Metrics:** View skill execution metrics and history with `hermes insights` or `/insights`. Raw data is tracked in `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`.

---

### 7. Security & Vulnerability Reporting

Do not post sensitive security vulnerabilities to public GitHub issues. Submit security reports via:
- **GitHub Security Advisory:** [Submit Advisory](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new)
- **Email:** `security@nousresearch.com`
